**Sikhae (식해)** – a classic Korean “raw‑fish” dish that’s all about freshness, simple seasoning, and a delicious dipping sauce. Below is a step‑by‑step guide to make a traditional, restaurant‑style sikhae at home. --- ## 1. Gather Your Ingredients | Category | Typical Items | Notes | |----------|---------------|-------| | **Seafood** | • Fresh sashimi‑grade fish (tuna, yellowtail, snapper, etc.)
• Shrimp, squid, octopus, mussels, clams, scallops | Use only fish that’s been handled properly and labeled “sashimi grade.” | | **Vegetables & Garnish** | • Thinly sliced cucumber
• Thinly sliced radish (daikon)
• Thinly sliced onion
• Thinly sliced green onion
• Thinly sliced red pepper (optional)
• Sesame seeds | These add crunch and color. | | **Sauce** | • Soy sauce (tamari for gluten‑free)
• Rice vinegar
• Sesame oil
• Gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
• Gochujang (optional, for heat)
• Sugar or honey
• Garlic (minced)
• Chili oil (optional) | Adjust heat to taste. | | **Optional Extras** | • Kimchi (for a spicy kick)
• Pickled vegetables | Adds depth and contrast. | > **Tip:** If you’re unsure about the freshness of your fish, ask the fishmonger for sashimi‑grade cuts or buy pre‑cut sashimi from a reputable market. --- ## 2. Prepare the Seafood 1. **Clean & Slice** - Rinse the fish under cold water, pat dry. - Slice into thin, bite‑size pieces (about 1–2 mm thick). - For shrimp, peel, devein, and slice lengthwise. - For squid, cut into rings; for octopus, slice into thin strips. 2. **Season Lightly** - Toss the sliced fish with a pinch of salt and a splash of rice vinegar to keep it fresh and slightly acidic. - Let sit for 5–10 minutes in the fridge. 3. **Arrange** - On a chilled platter or individual bowls, arrange the fish in a fan‑like pattern. - Layer different types of seafood together for visual appeal. --- ## 3. Make the Dipping Sauce (Sikhae Sauce) | Ingredient | Amount (per 1 cup of sauce) | Purpose | |------------|-----------------------------|---------| | Soy sauce | ½ cup | Base flavor | | Rice vinegar | ¼ cup | Brightness & acidity | | Sesame oil | 1 tbsp | Nutty aroma | | Gochugaru | 1 tsp (adjust) | Heat | | Gochujang | 1 tsp (optional) | Sweet‑spicy depth | | Sugar or honey | 1 tsp | Balance | | Minced garlic | 1 tsp | Aroma | | Chili oil | 1 tsp (optional) | Extra heat | | Sesame seeds | 1 tsp | Texture & garnish | **Instructions** 1. In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, gochugaru, gochujang, sugar, garlic, and chili oil until smooth. 2. Taste and adjust: more vinegar for tang, more sugar for sweetness, more gochugaru for heat. 3. Sprinkle sesame seeds on top before serving. --- ## 4. Add Vegetables & Garnish - Arrange thin cucumber, radish, onion, green onion, and optional red pepper around the fish. - Sprinkle a few sesame seeds over everything for a subtle crunch. - If you like, add a small side of kimchi or pickled vegetables for contrast. --- ## 5. Serve 1. **Plate** – Use a shallow, wide bowl or a wooden platter. 2. **Sauce** – Place the dipping sauce in a small bowl on the side. 3. **Enjoy** – Dip each piece of fish into the sauce before eating. 4. **Pair** – Traditionally served with steamed rice, kimchi, and a light broth (e.g., *guk* or *jigae*) on the side. --- ## 6. Safety & Tips | Issue | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Freshness** | Buy sashimi‑grade fish from a reputable source. | | **Cross‑contamination** | Use separate cutting boards for raw fish and other foods. | | **Temperature** | Keep fish chilled (≤ 4 °C) until ready to serve. | | **Allergies** | Some people may be allergic to shellfish; adjust accordingly. | | **Flavor Variations** | Add a splash of citrus (lemon or lime) to the sauce for extra brightness. | | **Presentation** | A clean, minimalist arrangement looks elegant and highlights the colors of the fish. | --- ### Quick Recipe Summary | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Slice sashimi‑grade fish & seafood thinly. | | 2 | Toss with salt & rice vinegar; chill. | | 3 | Arrange on a chilled platter. | | 4 | Whisk sauce ingredients together. | | 5 | Add sliced veggies & garnish. | | 6 | Serve with sauce on the side. | Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a refreshing, light dish that showcases the natural flavors of fresh seafood—perfect for a summer meal or a special occasion.
